verdict.rationale: Lium documents a public REST API with an OpenAPI spec at lium.io/api/openapi.json. Named endpoints include `POST /executors/rent-by-spec` and `GET /executors`, alongside stable error codes, scoped API keys with server-enforced budgets, and an agent guide stating everything can be done without a browser. The probe's 404s were on docs.lium.io paths, not the documented lium.io/api/openapi.json, so they do not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on confirmation that the documented OpenAPI spec and endpoints are reachable and work as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
**`error.code`** is stable. Branch on it, not on the message. **`error.hint`** says what to do next.
API keys with scopes and per-key daily, monthly and lifetime USD budgets enforced by the server
